description.narrative: Rehabilitation of Hale Hydro Power Plant in Tanga Region in Tanzania encompassing replacement of one generating unit (10,5 MW), partial renovation of the second unit plus comprehensive rehabilitation of civil, hydraulic and electromechanical equipment and the winding of Songo songo substation

Upprustning av Hale vattenkraftstation i Tanga region i Tanzania inkl byte av en generator (10,5 MW), delvis renovering av den andra generatorn, samt upprustning av utrustning och songo songo transformatorcentralen.

The main objective of the project is to provide renewable energy for poverty reduction. The specific objective is to ensure another 30-40 years power supply from the Hale hydropower station to the national grid, which includes improved overall operational and safety aspects of the hydropower plant. Hale power station is owned and operated by the national utility company Tanzania Electric Supply Company, Tanesco.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
The project is divided into two main lots. Lot 1, covering the access road, access tunnel, and associated civil works, was successfully completed and handed over in April 2024. The contractor has fulfilled its obligations, and payments are nearly complete, with approximately 98% of the contract value already paid. Lot 2 covers the rehabilitation of the powerhouse electromechanical systems, hydraulic steel structures, transformers, substation equipment, control and protection systems, and reinforcement of the headrace and tailrace tunnels. As of 30 May 2026, overall progress for Lot 2 stands at 82%.
Several key milestones have been achieved. The new access road and access tunnel are fully completed. The replacement of the powerhouse and gantry cranes has also been completed. Rehabilitation of hydraulic steel structures and construction of the switchgear building are approximately 95% complete. Installation of cooling systems, drainage systems, and plant control systems is progressing well, while generator, transformer, and substation equipment installation continues on site.
Current focus is on accelerating installation activities and ensuring timely delivery of the remaining outstanding equipment. The key items still awaiting delivery are the DC systems and certain 132 kV substation components, including circuit breakers and surge arresters. Close monitoring of shipping and logistics is underway to avoid further delays.
The supervising consultant, SWECO International AB in joint venture with Energy Infratech, continues to provide technical supervision, contract administration, payment certification, progress monitoring, safety oversight, and reporting support.
In general, the project has reached an advanced stage with major civil works completed and most rehabilitation activities well underway. While additional tunnel reinforcement works have extended the schedule, the project remains focused on achieving completion by July 2026 and delivering a modernized, more reliable, and sustainable hydropower facility that will strengthen electricity supply in Tanzania.
In summary, the project is progressing well and remains on a broadly positive trajectory. While the objectives are achievable within the intervention period, this will depend on maintaining momentum in the remaining works, particularly electromechanical installation and system integration and actively managing emerging risks over the final implementation phase.
